title: Turkey Promotes NATO Unity Agenda Ahead of July Ankara Summit
detail: Turkey's Foreign Ministry issued public statements on May 20, 2026, outlining Ankara's agenda for the NATO Summit it will host on July 7–8, 2026 — the first-ever NATO summit held in Turkey. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated Turkey will urge allies to 'reaffirm the alliance's unity and integrity' at the Ankara summit. Turkey is expected to advocate for stronger transatlantic defense industry cooperation and potential expansion of Indo-Pacific partner engagement at the ministerial level. Hosting the summit is seen as a significant diplomatic rehabilitation for Ankara after years of tensions with NATO allies over the S-400 purchase, F-35 expulsion, and relations with Russia.

media.caption: Turkey prepares to host NATO Summit in Ankara — July 2026
